audit_notes: 1) Positivity/bounds: all parameters are positive, within their stated bounds and physically standard (4 mm float glass, 12 mm argon cavity, k_glass=1.0, k_Ar=0.018 W/m/K, T_in=20 C, T_out=-10 C, EN 673-type film coefficients h_in=8, h_out=25 W/m^2/K). No adjustment required. 2) Model consistency: the formulated PDE uses a homogenized (series) through-thickness conductivity: x is normalized by the total thickness L=2*t_g+w=0.020 m and y by H=1.0 m, giving d2T/dx2 + (L/H)^2 d2T/dy2 = 0 with Robin coefficients Bi = h*R_cond, R_cond = 2 t_g/k_g + w/k_gas = 0.6747 m^2K/W. This reproduces the surface temperatures and heat flux of the layered stack exactly but replaces the piecewise (glass/gas/glass) interior profile by a linear one; the spacer_conductivity parameter is not used (top/bottom are adiabatic), so the edge-of-glass cold bridge is NOT captured and the solution is y-independent. Closed-form reference: R_total = 1/25 + 0.6747 + 1/8 = 0.8397 m^2K/W, U = 1.191 W/m^2/K, q = 35.73 W/m^2, outer glass surface 264.58 K (-8.57 C), inner glass surface 288.68 K (15.53 C); ~23.8 K of the 30 K drop is across the gas cavity. Inner surface stays above the dew point of 20 C / 50% RH air (~9.3 C) -> no condensation at center-of-glass. 3) Dimensionless numbers: Bi_out = h_out*R_cond = 16.87, Bi_in = h_in*R_cond = 5.40; cavity Rayleigh number Ra_w = g*beta*dT*w^3/(nu*alpha) ~ 6.5e3 with cavity aspect ratio H/w ~ 83: this is in the conduction/weak-convection regime (Nu ~ 1.0-1.2 per ElSherbiny-type tall-cavity correlations), so the pure-conduction gas assumption slightly under-predicts U (by up to ~15%). Geometric anisotropy (L/H)^2 = 4e-4 makes the PDE nearly 1D in x; the steep Robin coefficients and tiny y-coefficient make a PINN stiff, so the closed-form solution should be used as the reference. 4) Simulation coefficient: overall center-of-glass U-value = 1.191 W/m^2/K. 5) Solver: 2D PDE -> 'pinn' (validated against the analytical 1D series solution, which is the exact solution of this formulation). 6) Stress check: thermal loads only; the temperature drop across each pane is ~0.29 K (q*t_g/k_g), giving negligible through-thickness thermal stress (sigma ~ E*alpha*dT/2 ~ 70e9*9e-6*0.3/2 ~ 0.1 MPa << ~40 MPa annealed-glass design strength). Center-to-edge thermal stress with a warm-edge spacer is also well within limits. Temperatures (-10 to 20 C) are far below any glass or sealant limits. Performance gain is defined as heat-loss reduction vs. single 4 mm glazing (U_single = 5.92 W/m^2/K): 1 - 1.191/5.92 = 79.9%.
